seoTitle: Free Binary to Text and Text to Binary Converter
metaDescription: Convert text to 8-bit binary and binary back to text using UTF-8. Handles accents and emoji. Free, instant and runs in your browser.
intro: Turn text into groups of 8-bit binary, or paste ones and zeros and read the message. It works on UTF-8 bytes, so non-English characters come out correctly.
why:
Binary conversion is a staple of computing homework, puzzle hunts, CTF challenges and quick checks of how a character is stored. Doing it by hand means looking up codes and padding bits, and it is easy to drop a digit halfway through.

This tool converts each UTF-8 byte of your text to eight bits, separated by spaces. Going back, it ignores everything except 0 and 1, regroups the digits into bytes and decodes them. If the number of bits is not a multiple of eight, you are told so rather than given garbage. It all happens locally.
howTo: Choose "text to binary" or "binary to text" as the direction.
Paste the text, or the binary digits, into the Input box.
Copy the result from the output box.

faq.q: Why are there 8 bits per character?
faq.a: Each UTF-8 byte is shown as 8 bits. Basic English letters take one byte, so one group of 8. Accented letters and symbols use two to four bytes, so they appear as several groups.

faq.q: What if my binary has no spaces?
faq.a: That is fine. The decoder drops everything that is not a 0 or 1 and then splits the digits into groups of eight, so spaced and unspaced input both work.

faq.q: Why do I get an error about the length?
faq.a: The number of binary digits must be a multiple of 8. A missing or extra digit shifts every byte after it, so the tool refuses instead of guessing. Count the digits or look for a trimmed first or last group.

faq.q: Can it show 7-bit ASCII or 16-bit values?
faq.a: No. It always uses 8-bit bytes of UTF-8. For other bases or two's complement of whole numbers, use the Number Base Converter.
